audits.title: AN AUDIT OF THE MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE PAIN IN CHILDREN.
audits.standard: Locally developed standards: timely analgesia and reassessment after pain score in 80%; 4-hourly pain scores on regular analgesia in 80%; naloxone co-prescribed with strong opioids in 90%
audits.setting: Paediatric wards excluding intensive care and day surgery, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Analgesia given in the same hour for 58% (34/59) severe and 30% (28/92) mild/moderate pain scores; reassessment within 60 minutes after 52% (37/71) and 34% (31/92) of doses; 83% (15/18) on regular analgesia assessed 4-hourly; 45% on strong opioids had no naloxone.

audits.other_findings: Only hourly pain score documentation was seen; revised guideline and medical and nurse training are planned.
audits.citation: Sidhu J, Tickner N. AN AUDIT OF THE MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE PAIN IN CHILDREN. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.11. PMID: 27540189.

audits.title: An institutional quality improvement initiative for pain management for pediatric cancer inpatients.
audits.standard: Institutional pain standard of care (pain assessment; effective treatment to <=4/10 within one hour)
audits.setting: Inpatient units, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis
audits.intervention: Institutional quality improvement initiative with repeated chart audits and comprehensive pain management guidelines

cycle2.result: Compliance consistently greater than 90%; 66% of patients with significant pain treated effectively within one hour.

audits.other_findings: Lack of documented pain reassessment within one hour persisted throughout (22%).
audits.citation: Oakes LL, Anghelescu DL, Windsor KB, Barnhill PD. An institutional quality improvement initiative for pain management for pediatric cancer inpatients. J Pain Symptom Manage. 2008;35(6):656-669. doi:10.1016/j.jpainsymman.2007.07.008. PMID: 18329841.

audits.title: An audit of pain management following pediatric day surgery at British Columbia Children's Hospital.

cycle1.result: Pain reports and scores significantly higher at home than in hospital (P<0.01); good pain control commonly achieved after surgery.

audits.other_findings: Recommends more multimodal analgesia, standardised written discharge instructions and surgery-specific analgesia guidelines.
audits.citation: Shum S, Lim J, Page T, Lamb E, Gow J, Ansermino JM, et al.. An audit of pain management following pediatric day surgery at British Columbia Children's Hospital. Pain Res Manag. 2012;17(5):328-334. doi:10.1155/2012/541751. PMID: 23061083.

audits.title: Pain assessment and management in paediatric oncology: a cross-sectional audit.
audits.standard: International recommendations for paediatric pain management
audits.setting: Children's Cancer Centre, Royal Children's Hospital, Melbourne; inpatients

cycle1.result: Pain present in 146/258 (57%); pain recorded by health professionals in 75/146 (51%); non-drug methods in 38/146 (26%); pain appropriately managed in 65/76 (87%) by the Pain Management Index.

audits.other_findings: Opioids were the mainstay (56%); poor documentation limited assessment of effectiveness.
audits.citation: Plummer K, McCarthy M, McKenzie I, Newall F, Manias E. Pain assessment and management in paediatric oncology: a cross-sectional audit. J Clin Nurs. 2017;26(19-20):2995-3006. doi:10.1111/jocn.13643. PMID: 27862499.

audits.title: An audit of paediatric pain prevalence, intensity, and treatment at a South African tertiary hospital.

cycle1.result: 87% had pain during admission; 25% had pain at time of study (median score 6/10); only 16% of charts had documented pain intensity scores.

audits.other_findings: Worst pain was from needle procedures (34%); authors state the audit will be repeated as part of a QI initiative.
audits.citation: Velazquez Cardona C, Rajah C, Mzoneli YN, Friedrichsdorf SJ, Campbell F, Cairns C, et al.. An audit of paediatric pain prevalence, intensity, and treatment at a South African tertiary hospital. Pain Rep. 2019;4(6):e789. doi:10.1097/pr9.0000000000000789. PMID: 31984294.

audits.title: Cross-sectional study of pediatric pain prevalence, assessment, and treatment at a Canadian tertiary hospital.
audits.setting: Paediatric ward, paediatric ED and maternal services, tertiary hospital in Saskatoon (single-day audits)

cycle1.result: Pain prevalence 75% to 88%; moderate to severe pain 78% ward, 65% ED, 55% maternal services; pain assessment documented 93% ward, 13% ED, 0% maternal services.

audits.other_findings: Documented pain scores underestimated patient report by a mean 4.5/10; needle pokes were the commonest cause of worst pain.
audits.citation: Senger A, Bryce R, McMahon C, Baerg K. Cross-sectional study of pediatric pain prevalence, assessment, and treatment at a Canadian tertiary hospital. Can J Pain. 2021;5(1):172-182. doi:10.1080/24740527.2021.1961081. PMID: 34616998.

audits.title: Parental involvement in postoperative pain management among children in a urology ward: A best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: Fifteen evidence-based audit criteria for parental involvement in postoperative pain management
audits.setting: Paediatric urology ward, Children's Hospital of Soochow University
audits.intervention: Evidence-based strategies targeting identified barriers (best practice implementation project).

cycle2.result: Compliance improved for all criteria; three criteria reached 100%.

audits.citation: Yang JX, Zhang WY, Huang HH, Jiang WT, Zhou YF, Gu Y, et al.. Parental involvement in postoperative pain management among children in a urology ward: A best practice implementation project. Nurs Open. 2023;10(5):3042-3051. doi:10.1002/nop2.1551. PMID: 36566489.
